explanation: Draw a uniform number in [0,1), then subtract consecutive probabilities until the remainder becomes negative. Return the associated value; the final value owns the remaining tail.
timeComplexity: O(n) per call: at most n−1 probability subtractions. The bound includes all probability processing performed anew on each draw, rather than assuming precomputed endpoints.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. The linear scan keeps only a draw and running threshold; binary-search variants retain n prefix endpoints.
attribution: Original C++ implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed weighted-random contract and repository-authored C# algorithm. The existing million-draw statistical protocol and 5σ acceptance bounds are preserved. No upstream reference implementation was modified.
correctness: Before subtracting probability i, the remainder equals the draw minus the earlier probabilities. A negative result means the draw lies inside interval i; otherwise that interval is skipped. Thus each interval has its specified probability mass.
walkthrough: For values [4,9] with probabilities [0.25,0.75], draws below 0.25 return 4 and draws from 0.25 onward return 9. A draw of 0.6 therefore returns 9; repeated draws select 9 three times as often on average. JSON arguments are [values,probabilities]. Observed true validates repeated samples; the callable returns one value. Finite samples do not prove exact randomness.
edgeCases: One value is always selected when its probability is one.
The validator checks repeated samples rather than one fixed output.
